messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: PC prior for Matern models
parts:
It went to a new direction and I started a new thread.

On 11/08/2017 12:57, Guiming Wang wrote:

Regarding the PC prior, I had difficulties of choosing a value for u inside param=c(u, 0.01).  Similarly, in the case of PC Matern priors for SPDE, I had difficulties of specifying the range and variance parameters and their tail probabilities.  In a case, I used param=c(100, 0.01) as a PC prior for Matern’s standard deviation and had the 95% CI excluding zero (making biological senses); however, the DIC of the spde model with the PC prior was much greater than that of the default matern priors.

You can plot to see if it fits what you do believe is your prior knowledge. The PC-prior is made to find 'no effect' when it is the fact. A side effect is that it does shrink. 

 Any suggestions of the parameter specification of PC priors (such as a specification may work for most cases)? Or any other articles may be helpful?  Thanks.

Maybe we have to bear in mind that a prior for a particular problem has to be particular. The PC-prior framework was build under principles and can be computed in a interpretable scale to help you choosing the prior. The PC-prior for Gaussian random fields is in https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00256

Elias

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC prior for Matern models
parts:
The credible region for sigma based on lower and upper quantiles of the posterior will never contain zero. Testing for "no effect" by checking if the CR for sigma contains zero or not is therefore meaningless.

Finn

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC prior for Matern models
parts:
Not completely sure what this is about, but
- The DIC is not a good measure for spatial models (p \approx n)
- Personally, I prefer to set the median (instead of the 0.01 quantile)
- Testing for no-effect is very difficult, as how you design the test depends on what you mean

## Testing for no effect
What should happen if the data is indifferent to the use of a model component? (I.e. sigma is not identifiable from the data) Should the test give "model component not needed" (sigma=0), or "model component not rejected" (sigma != 0) ?

I would go with prior-posterior plots of sigma, unless you have specific requirements.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC prior for Matern models
parts:
I think you will see a random plot like that anyway, since the "s" is arbitrarily located in space...?

For a time series (or nonlinear covariate) you should see some structure, but space is 2-dimensionsal.

The point I was making was about the design of the "test", since you have to decide what outcome you want in cases with a flat likelihood. The usual is to say "cannot reject null hypothesis", but this depends on whether null is "effect" or "no effect". If null is "no effect", then you will conclude "no effect" from a flat likelihood, which may or may not be reasonable.

Kind regards,
Haakon
